airport.name: JMSDF Atsugi Air Base / Naval Air Facility Atsugi

summary: Naval Air Facility Atsugi is a joint military airbase operated by the Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force (JMSDF) and the United States Navy, located in Kanagawa Prefecture near Ayase and Yamato. It serves as a major hub for maritime patrol, helicopter operations, and serves as the home base for the US Navy's Carrier Air Wing 5 when deployed to the region. The base also hosts elements of Helicopter Maritime Strike Squadron and supports anti-submarine warfare missions in the western Pacific.
faqs:
Q: Is NAF Atsugi open to civilian travelers?
A: No, this is a military installation and is not a commercial airport with passenger services for the general public.

Q: Who operates the airbase?
A: It is jointly operated by the Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force (JMSDF) and the United States Navy.

Q: What is the base used for?
A: It supports maritime patrol, anti-submarine warfare, helicopter operations, and serves as a deployment base for US Navy carrier air wings operating in the Pacific.

Q: Are there any museums or public areas on base?
A: There may be limited access events, but the base is generally restricted to authorized military personnel and their dependents.
transport_tips: Public access is limited since this is a military facility. The nearest train stations are Sagami-Kōya on the Odakyu Line or Nakayama on the JR Yokohama Line, both requiring a short taxi or bus ride. Travelers associated with the base typically use a personal vehicle, military shuttle, or authorized transport arranged through their unit.
local_tip: If you're on official business, remember that base entry requires a valid military ID or prior visitor authorization processed through your sponsoring unit, so arrange paperwork well before your visit.
